# `.pix3anim` — flipbook animation resources

A `.pix3anim` is **JSON**: a set of named clips, each a list of frames. `AnimatedSprite2D`
plays one: `animationResourcePath: res://…/foo.pix3anim`, `currentClip`, `isPlaying`,
`sizeMode`, `freeOnFinish` (the node's properties are in `pix3-nodes`; `AnimatedSprite3D` takes
its own `frames` list instead). The loader
reads the resource and every frame texture it names, also for a node that arrives through a
prefab or `scene.instantiate`. **Every field may be omitted**: the loader fills in the default
in the tables below, so hand-write only what you mean.

Keep a flipbook in its own folder, the frames beside it — `sprites/<name>/<name>.pix3anim` +
`sprites/<name>/<clip>_<nnnn>.png` (the editor's Sprite Editor writes and reads that layout and
shows the folder as one item). Nothing enforces it: any `res://` path works.

## Create one and bind it

The editor does not create a `.pix3anim` (its inspector binds an existing one); you write it:

1. Frames into one folder: `sprites/<name>/<clip>_0001.png`, `<clip>_0002.png`, … (or SVGs —
   by the rules of AGENTS.md rule 5; `pix3 validate` checks the frames a `.pix3anim` names like
   a scene's sprites: `E_SVG_*`, reported on the `.pix3anim`).
2. `sprites/<name>/<name>.pix3anim`: `version`, `texturePath: ""` and one clip per animation,
   each frame naming its image — the example under "Two modes" below; leave out every field
   whose default (the tables) is what you want.
3. Bind it on the `AnimatedSprite2D` node:

   ```yaml
   - id: coin-spin
     type: AnimatedSprite2D
     name: Coin Spin
     properties:
       width: 96
       height: 96
       animationResourcePath: res://sprites/coin/coin.pix3anim
       currentClip: spin
       isPlaying: true
   ```

   A script switches clips with `sprite.play('spin')`.
4. `pix3 check`: a wrong `animationResourcePath` is `E_MISSING_RESOURCE`, a frame path that
   points nowhere `E_MISSING_FRAME`, a file that is not JSON `E_ANIM_JSON`; then
   `pix3 smoke <the scene>`.

## Two modes

- **Sequence** (one image per frame — the usual case): every frame sets `texturePath`; the
  top-level `texturePath` stays `""`.
- **Spritesheet**: the top-level `texturePath` is the sheet; each frame leaves its own
  `texturePath` empty and sets the UV rect `offset` + `repeat` (fractions of the sheet). Both
  default to `{ "x": 0, "y": 0 }`, which samples nothing — required in this mode.

```json
{
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "texturePath": "",
  "clips": [
    {
      "name": "burst",
      "fps": 30,
      "loop": false,
      "frames": [
        { "texturePath": "res://sprites/burst/burst_0001.png" },
        { "texturePath": "res://sprites/burst/burst_0002.png", "durationMultiplier": 2 }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

## The fields

Types are the runtime's (`AnimationResource.ts`); "Omitted →" is what the loader fills in. A
field marked `?` is optional in the file format itself.

### `AnimationResource`

The file.

| Field | Type | Omitted → | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `version` | `string` | `"1.0.0"` | The only version; copy it |
| `texturePath` | `string` | `""` | Spritesheet mode: `res://` of the sheet. Sequence mode: `""` |
| `clips` | `AnimationClip[]` | `[]` | Clip names must be unique — scripts address clips by name |

### `AnimationClip`

| Field | Type | Omitted → | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | `clip-<n>` (1-based position) | What `currentClip` and `sprite.play(name)` use |
| `frames` | `AnimationFrame[]` | `[]` | In play order |
| `fps` | `number` | `12` | Frames per second; positive |
| `loop` | `boolean` | `true` | `false`: holds the last frame, `isPlaying` turns false, the node emits `animation-finished` (`freeOnFinish: true` then removes it) |
| `playbackMode` | `AnimationPlaybackMode` | `"normal"` | `"normal"` or `"ping-pong"` |

### `AnimationFrame`

| Field | Type | Omitted → | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `textureIndex` | `number` | `0` | Legacy; leave it 0 |
| `offset` | `AnimationVector2` | `{"x":0,"y":0}` | Spritesheet mode: UV origin of the frame in the sheet |
| `repeat` | `AnimationVector2` | `{"x":0,"y":0}` | Spritesheet mode: UV size of the frame in the sheet |
| `durationMultiplier` | `number` | `1` | This frame lasts `durationMultiplier / fps` seconds |
| `anchor` | `AnimationVector2` | `{"x":0.5,"y":0.5}` | The point of the frame (0–1, **y from the top**) that lands on the node's position — the feet for a character |
| `texturePath` | `string` | `""` | Sequence mode: `res://` of this frame's image |
| `boundingBox` | `AnimationBoundingBox` | `{"x":0,"y":0,"width":0,"height":0}` | Frame rect in source pixels |
| `collisionPolygon` | `AnimationPolygonPoint[]` | `[]` | Optional outline in frame space |
| `events?` | `AnimationFrameEvent[]` | `[]` | Signals the node emits when play enters this frame |
| `sourceSize?` | `AnimationSize` | the `boundingBox` size | Pixel size of the frame image; `sizeMode: native` lays the node out from it (`0×0` = unknown → stretch) |
| `points?` | `AnimationFramePoint[]` | `[]` | Named sockets (a muzzle, a hand) that move across frames; `core:PointAttachment` parks a child on one |

### `AnimationVector2`

| Field | Type | Omitted → | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `x` | `number` | — | |
| `y` | `number` | — | |

### `AnimationBoundingBox`

| Field | Type | Omitted → | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `x` | `number` | — | From the frame's left edge, pixels |
| `y` | `number` | — | From the frame's top edge, pixels |
| `width` | `number` | — | |
| `height` | `number` | — | |

### `AnimationPolygonPoint`

| Field | Type | Omitted → | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `x` | `number` | — | |
| `y` | `number` | — | |

### `AnimationFrameEvent`

| Field | Type | Omitted → | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `signal` | `string` | — | Emitted on the node; an empty signal drops the event |
| `args` | `string` | — | Raw text, parsed when it fires (same convention as the keyframe event track) |

### `AnimationSize`

| Field | Type | Omitted → | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `width` | `number` | — | |
| `height` | `number` | — | |

### `AnimationFramePoint`

| Field | Type | Omitted → | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | — | Unique within the frame (the first wins) |
| `x` | `number` | — | 0–1 of the frame width |
| `y` | `number` | — | 0–1 of the frame height, from the top |
| `angle?` | `number` | — | Degrees, clockwise, 0 = pointing right |

`AnimationPlaybackMode` is `"normal" | "ping-pong"`.

## A character with variants and states

One `.pix3anim` whose clips are named `<variant>.<state>` (`sword.idle`, `sword.attack`,
`bow.idle`; a clip without the dot is a variant-less state such as `die`), an `AnimatedSprite2D`
prefab root with `sizeMode: native`, and `core:CharacterVisual2D` on it (`variant`, `state`).
Game code calls `playState('attack', { restart: true })` and `setVariant('bow')` and never spells
a clip name. Do not write it by hand — compile it from the frame images:

```bash
pix3 character-compile art/goblin.yaml --dry-run   # the plan
pix3 character-compile art/goblin.yaml             # sprites/goblin/…, scenes/prefabs/Goblin.pix3scene
```

```yaml
# art/goblin.yaml — frame paths are relative to this file; frames must be PNG
name: Goblin
anchor: { x: 0.5, y: 0.9 }   # the feet
clips:
  - { variant: sword, state: idle, fps: 10, frames: [sword/idle_1.png, sword/idle_2.png] }
  - { variant: sword, state: attack, fps: 15, sequence: sword/attack }  # sword/attack_<n>.png
  - { state: die, sequence: die/die }
```

It refuses to overwrite a file with other content (`--force` to replace) and prints the defaults
it chose (fps 12, one-shot `attack`/`die`/`hit`) as warnings. Then instance the prefab
(`instance: res://scenes/prefabs/Goblin.pix3scene`) and run `pix3 check`.
